resources.title: C-Roux4 4x4 Speedcubing Method (doc tab 'CR4 4x4 Speedcubing Method'; hub link text 'CriticalCubing's CR4 Tutorial')
resources.author: CriticalCubing (stated in the doc: '(by CriticalCubing)')
resources.level: Beginner to intermediate big-cube. It assumes the reader already solves 3x3 with Roux (FB, SB, CMLL, LSE) and can pair 4x4 centres and edges. There are no algs to learn.
resources.summary: A single-tab Google Doc (about 4.7 KB of text, plus 7 rendered 3D 4x4 state images, one per step). It explains CR4 (also called C-Roux4 or Critical-Roux4), a 4x4 method that reduces the cube to 3x3 while building the Roux First Block early, then finishes with normal Roux. There are 7 steps. (1) Two opposite centres, which are the FB and SB centres, so the L/R colours when white/yellow are on D/U. (2) First Block as a 1x3x4 block on L. The doc lists several ways to build it: pair DL and the 2 FB edges and then add corners; make a square and expand it; insert DL and then freestyle; or a line approach. The author prefers pairing the 3 edges first. (3) Two adjacent centres (on D and B) while pairing any edge into DB. (4) Pair 3 edges and park them in the R slice without breaking FB or the B centre, either freestyle or by pairing in DF. (5) The last two centres using inner-layer moves, so the R-slice edges are untouched and MU LSE-style TPS can be used. (6) Finish edge pairing: pair 2, then 2 more, and the last one pairs itself. (7) SB, CMLL, LSE, plus parity if any. Stated pros and cons: lots of freedom, highly intuitive, relies on M slices, and a move count comparable to other 4x4 methods. Two example solves give a scramble and step-commented solutions, each linked to an alg.cubing.net 4x4 replay. Parity is mentioned but no parity algs are given. No licence. Linked from rouxcubing.com BIG CUBES > BIG CUBE TUTORIALS > CR4.

resources.title: Bigcube Parity OLL/PLL and C(M)LL (hub link texts: 'TDM's Parity CMLL', 'Louis' parity CMLL algorithms')
resources.author: TDM / Louis according to the hub link texts, presumably Louis de Mendonça. The sheet itself names no author. It thanks 'Rob Yau (+ others) for most of the cool algs' and says 'Last updated: July 2025'.
resources.level: Advanced big-cube: the user is expected to know full CMLL and at least one OLL-parity alg
resources.summary: A Google Sheet with 6 visible tabs (About, OLL, PLL, C(M)LL, 4c, QR) and 4 hidden tabs that only the xlsx export shows (OLL (old), PLL (no images), CLL + edge control, CLL E2 + parity). All were saved. The About tab defines four named single-dedge-flip OLL-parity algs that the other tabs use as macros: DP (double parity), LP (Lucas parity), BDP (back DP) and BLP (back LP). For each it says whether it flips UF or UB, gives equivalences (DP U2 = U2 BDP, LP U2 = U2 BLP) and explains that '(P)' means any parity alg with the flipped edge in UF. A UB-flipping alg can be used from a U2-offset angle, and the AUFs after it may change. '(cancel)' marks a cancellation, alternatives are in cell notes, and every case has at least one Lucas-parity alg. The Roux-relevant core is the C(M)LL tab: 43 rows (the 42 CMLL cases plus solved corners). Each row gives an alg that solves the corners and fixes OLL parity together, usually a short CMLL/OLL-style trigger plus a (P) macro at a stated AUF. Rows are grouped by the 8 corner-orientation sets: O (solved/adj/diag), S, A, T, L, U, H and P (Pi). The set headers carry recognition hints, for example the oriented corner location, or the angle from which a named CO alg would solve orientation. Each case has a nickname (sune, nik, apple, Lapple, Ashit, sexysledge, T long/short, goodadj, front/back comm, checkerboard, bars, E2, pure, good, bad, diag and so on). A '*' marks algs that do not preserve F2L. These use wide/M-slice moves, which I infer are still F2B-safe for Roux. 37 C(M)LL cells have notes with alternative algs. The 4c tab links to TDM's Parity 4c doc, says its algs are 'bad and I doubt they're worth learning', and recommends using DFDB recognition to force either a skip or an opposite swap on U and then doing parity. The OLL tab (54 OLL-parity cases with 4x4 top-view images, 18 notes) and the PLL tab (22 PLL-parity cases with images, names and some recognition notes, 18 notes) are for reduction/CFOP last layer and are not Roux. QR holds one QR-code image, which I did not decode. Hidden drafts: CLL + edge control has 43 CLL cases, each marked 'CLL' or 'E2'/'HAX', with a few edge-state variants. CLL E2 + parity is an incomplete enumeration of 192 last-layer edge states in 4 groups of 48 (labelled 1!p, 1p, 3!p, 3p), with a fill counter and ZBLL/OLLCP notes. No licence.

resources.title: Bigcube parity 4c (hub link text 'TDM's Parity 4c')
resources.author: TDM according to the hub link text, presumably Louis de Mendonça. The doc names no author.
resources.level: Advanced big-cube Roux (LSE with PLL/edge-swap parity)
resources.summary: A single-tab Google Doc (about 2 KB). The intro says the algs are written for 4x4 and work on bigger cubes by substituting wide moves (for example Rw -> 3Rw on 6x6). It describes itself as an attempt at a complete list that also documents simple known tricks, warns that many solutions are probably not optimal, puts the worst ones in italics, and asks for better solutions. The 'Oriented centres' section has 24 cases, each with 1 to 3 algs; 9 cases have an italic (worst) alg. The 'Misoriented centres' section is empty except for a note asking for contributions. Cases are named by which two M-slice edges are swapped: U swap (UF/UB), D swap, F swap, B swap, and the diagonal UFDB and UBDF swaps. Each has '+ M2' / 'M2 +' variants for the centre offset. Four-cycle cases are named O / O' (+M2), or by composite names that describe the front/back or top/bottom halves in 3x3 4c terms (for example 'Front U2M2U2, back E2M'E2M'). My inference: 24 = the 12 odd permutations of the four M-slice edges (6 swaps + 6 four-cycles) x 2 centre states (solved or M2), so the oriented-centre set is complete. The algs are built from a standard 4x4 edge-swap parity alg conjugated with M/U setups, some written in [A: B] conjugate notation. The Parity CMLL sheet's 4c tab calls these algs 'bad' and recommends forcing a U swap or skip through DFDB recognition instead. No licence.

resources.title: 'im the twizzler baby' (sheet title); tab '50 2h roux example solves (assuming best fb+ss)'; hub link texts 'Eff's Example Solves' / 'eff's Example Solves (2H)'
resources.author: Eff, according to the hub link texts (Eff also appears in the hubs' list of Rouxer YouTube channels)
resources.level: Intermediate to advanced 2H: it uses EOLRb, CMLLEO, EOFBb and cancellations, and has a 38 STM average
resources.summary: One tab with 50 two-handed Roux example solves. The tab title says they assume the best FB+SS, so FB and SS are idealised rather than inspection-realistic. Columns: scramble; a link to the alpha.twizzle.net editor with the scramble as setup and the solution split by step with // comments; then move counts per step: fb, sb (which includes SS), cmll, lse and total. Move counts are in STM and include AUFs. An averages row gives FB 5.98, SS+SB 12.04, CMLL 9.82, LSE 10.50 and total 38.34. A 'woaj' row gives the per-column minimums (3, 6, 0, 0) and their sum (9). Ranges: FB 3-8, SS+SB 6-16, CMLL 0-15 (2 skips), LSE 0-15 (1 skip), total 26-46. The step labels in the comments are inspection, FB, SS, SB, CMLL, CMLL(EO), EOLRb (31 times), 4c (34), LSE, EOFBb, pseudopair, 'with dot avoidance', 'cancelling into' and 'with 4c influence'. There are 13 standalone notes on ergonomics and choices: 'eido' the U2' with the thumb on top, M' with the right ring finger, avoid a risky regrip, finger-trick M as r' R, skip an available OLLCP, choose an SS that preserves the next pair, pick a CMLL because it gives a better EOLRb. No algs are taught and there is no licence.

resources.summary: A Google Sheet index of YouTube example-solve videos for every WCA event, with 18 tabs: 3x3, 2x2, 4x4, 5x5, 6x6, 7x7, 3BLD, FMC, OH, WF, Clock, Megaminx, Pyraminx, Skewb, Square-1, 4BLD, 5BLD and MBLD. All were fetched. Each tab groups video links by method, with columns 'Estimated Global' (the solver's level), 'Solver' and sometimes 'Extra info' (for example 'Cyotheking Style'). Most tabs contain only a method heading and no videos: 5x5-7x7 Reduction, 3BLD and 4BLD 3-Style, FMC Various, WF CFOP, Clock Pochmann, Megaminx asking for help, Pyraminx V First, Skewb NS. Roux content: the 3x3 tab's Roux section has 14 entries (13 unique videos, because Iuri Grangeiro's is listed twice with 9.8 and 10.1): 10 by Kian Mansour, 1 by Vincent Wong (the video is now on the Kangaroux channel), 1 by Kavin Tangtartharakul, 1 by Iuri Grangeiro and 1 by Yuval Porat (a sub-20 solver). The OH tab's Roux section has 8 Kian Mansour OH example-solve videos. Everything else is not Roux: CFOP (1 3x3, 1 OH), ZZ (6), 2x2 EG/CLL (8), 4x4 Yau (17), Square-1 (1), 5BLD (2) and an MBLD improvement video. I checked all 21 Roux video IDs through YouTube oEmbed on 2026-10-29 and all are live. The Google redirect timestamps in some links point to the sheet being built around early 2019 (my inference). No licence.

resources.author: Maintainer not stated. Named contributors: Kian Mansour (analysis of Sean Villanueva's 5.98 average), Iuri Grangeiro, Vincent Wong, Louis de Mendonça, Pyjam, Ryan Peh and Antonio Kam.
resources.level: Intermediate to advanced (fast 2H and OH Roux solves, including world-class averages)
resources.summary: A Google Sheet with 4 tabs. 'Info' gives the title, says to use the tabs, and says each solve's comments are cell notes on its link. 'Described Reconstructions/Example Solves' has Sean Villanueva's 5.98 average (5 solves). It links to Kian Mansour's analysis video with per-solve timestamps, and the cell notes hold each solve's step-commented reconstruction with ETM and TPS. It also has Sean's 4.98 single, linked to Iuri Grangeiro's breakdown video, plus a language column ('en'). 'Reconstructions' has 16 rows (8 2H, 7 OH, 1 unspecified): 15 alg.cubing.net recon links and 1 YouTube video. Solvers are Iuri Grangeiro, Ryan Peh, Antonio Kam, Ryan Peh + Antonio Kam, Vincent Wong, Louis de Mendonça and Pyjam. Remarks include 'Regripless solution', 'Sub-20 STM', 'F2B found by Ryan', 'LSE Skip (7.58)' and 'Strong SB Influencing'. 'Submit Solves' links a Google Form that was still accepting entries on 2026-10-29 (it asks for a type, then a video/example-solve link or text). The most reusable part is the technique-tag checkbox taxonomy, grouped by step. First Block: DL + 2 Pairs, Line-line 2x2x1 + pair, Line-Line, BL Edge fix, Non-Matching Centers, Premade Square. Second Block: Edge First, Pair First, Blockbuilding, Multislotting. CMLL: EO Influencing. LSE: Oriented Centers, Misoriented Centers, EOLRb (direct), EOBF. Tag use across the 16 reconstructions: Edge First 10, Oriented Centers 10, Blockbuilding 10, Line-Line 6, Line-line 2x2x1 + pair 6, Multislotting 6, DL + 2 Pairs 4, Misoriented Centers 4, EOLRb 3, Pair First 2, EO Influencing 2, EOBF 1. There are 22 solves in all, so the database is small and has not grown much. All 3 YouTube videos are live (oEmbed, 2026-10-29). No licence.
